== PS2 2.00 hidden Remote Control option page ==
''Suggested page: PS2 → OSDSYS → Hidden Options & Service Menus.''

In PlayStation 2 BIOS version 2.00 E (SCPH-70004), reverse engineering of <code>rom0:OSDSYS</code> reveals a hidden configuration page titled '''"Remote Control Off/On"'''. The page is reachable from the Version Information screen via a controller chord on port 2, but is gated by a MechaCon EEPROM configuration bit.

=== Trigger combination ===
# In the OSDSYS main menu, press '''Triangle''' to enter Version Information.
# Highlight the '''Console''' entry.
# On '''controller port 2, slot 0''', hold:
:'''Select + Start + L1 + L2 + R1 + R2''' (active-high digital mask <code>0x090F</code>).
# Routine <code>0x2266F0</code> tests:
:<code>(port2_buttons & 0x090F) == 0x090F</code>
#* There is '''no hold duration or sequential code'''; it evaluates as a subset bitmask on the current frame.
#* '''Port input-folding detail''': the pad poller at <code>0x208DB8</code> constructs each pad's state using its own high byte (Start/Select/D-pad) but an accumulated low byte (shoulders/face buttons) from earlier polled ports. Consequently, holding the shoulder buttons on port 1 while pressing Start + Select on port 2 also satisfies the condition [I].

=== Menu registration and display ===
* The hidden option record is registered at <code>0x206CC8</code>.
* It is placed after the ordinary list terminator, so it does not appear as a selectable line in the normal menu.
* When triggered, <code>0x224678</code> invokes builder <code>0x206AA8</code> with string ID <code>0x67</code> (<code>"Remote Control"</code>) and value ID <code>0x12</code> (editor strategy 2), presenting an '''Off / On''' toggle.
* This feature was not present in earlier revisions (1.00 J MCLOCK <code>0x605AC0</code>, 1.50 devkit <code>0x220D10</code>, or 1.60 <code>0x2215E0</code>).

=== Configuration bits and MechaCon gate ===
The hidden option is governed by three distinct bits in packed MechaCon configuration byte <code>0x13</code> (unpacked by <code>0x203A08</code>):

{| class="wikitable"
! Packed config byte !! Unpacked field !! Function in OSDSYS 2.00 E
|-
| '''Byte 0x13, bit 7''' || Config word 1, bit 2 (getter <code>0x204468</code>) || '''Hidden menu gate''': enables registration of the port 2 hidden option record at <code>0x206CC8</code>.
|-
| '''Byte 0x13, bit 6''' || Config word 1, bit 3 (getter <code>0x204428</code>) || '''Current setting''': stores Remote Control Off (0) vs On (1).
|-
| '''Byte 0x13, bit 5''' || Config word 1, bit 4 (getter <code>0x2044A8</code>) || '''Standard menu visibility''': controls whether the Remote Control option appears in the standard System Configuration menu.
|}

=== Reachability on retail hardware ===
In an authentic SCPH-70004 retail NVM dump, raw byte <code>0x2C4</code> (corresponding to packed byte <code>0x13</code>) holds value '''<code>0x20</code>''':
* Bit 5 is set (standard Remote Control item visible).
* Bit 7 is '''clear (0)''', meaning the hidden option gate is disabled in standard factory units.

Furthermore, during cold boot, OSDSYS <code>main</code> (<code>0x209EB8</code>) sends CDVD S-command RPC fno <code>0x30</code> with the inverse of the Remote Control setting. If the drive firmware responds with a status word containing <code>0x100</code>, the branch at <code>0x20A334</code> forcibly '''clears both the hidden gate (bit 7) and the ordinary menu bit (bit 5)'''.

The original purpose of this hidden page is believed to be factory provisioning or MechaCon production testing, rather than an end-user Easter egg.

''Source: [https://github.com/NamasteJasutin/PSXBootInspectionTool PSXBootInspectionTool], notes/research/hidden_input.md §1, §3.''
